chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If you intend to depart [from Mina] on one of the two days, you are not permitted to depart until the sun passes its zenith. If you delay until the last of the days of Tashriq, which is the final day of departure, there is no blame upon you regarding which hour you depart and throw [the pebbles], before or after the zenith. When you depart and reach al-Hasba', which is al-Batha', if you wish to stay for a short while, then indeed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to stay there, then mount and enter Mecca without sleeping in it.'

key_terms.التَّشْرِيق: The days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhul-Hijjah)
key_terms.الْبَطْحَاء: Al-Batha', another name for the area where the Prophet stayed

ai.seo_question: What are the specific time restrictions for leaving Mina after throwing the Jamarat?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal flexibility of the Hajj departure (*Nafar*) from Mina, distinguishing between the restricted timing of the first two Tashriq days and the unrestricted nature of the final day. It further highlights the Prophetic tradition of resting briefly at al-Hasba' (al-Batha') before entering Mecca, illustrating the balance between ritual obligation and practical ease in Shia jurisprudence.
